subject: Pilot acceptance criteria & performance validation playbook - OrbitHealth
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Ramos <alice@orbithealth.com>, OrbitHealth SRE <sre-team@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot acceptance criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Hi Alice / Tom / team,

Thanks again for the demo call this morning — great visibility into the production constraints. Per our conversation, I've put together a concise acceptance checklist and a proposed validation playbook so we can scope the dedicated pilot and sizing run. Can you confirm the targets below or flag any changes?

Pilot acceptance (what OrbitHealth will sign off on to call the pilot successful):
- P95 E2E latency for typical interactive prompt (avg 200 tokens): <= 250 ms (stable over 1h window)
- P99 E2E latency spike containment: <= 600 ms (no more than 0.5% of requests)
- Streaming incremental token latency (time between tokens) at steady-state: <= 55 ms
- Sustained throughput: 40 RPS (avg payload 150 tokens) for 30 minutes without degradation
- Concurrent sessions supported: 60 concurrent active sessions with KV cache enabled
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts): < 0.2% across the pilot window
- Cold-start tail: first-token latency after idle period (10m idle): <= 1.2s

Validation plan (high level):
1) Synthetic microbench: fixed-size prompts to validate per-GPU token/sec and incremental token latency.
2) Stateful streaming test: simulate interactive sessions with KV cache warm/cold cycles.
3) Soak test: 6–24h run at 50–70% reserved throughput to detect resource leaks/variance.
4) Failover and fallback validation: forced model fallback to quantized variant and cross-region routing test.

Proposed pilot hardware matrix to test: H100(80GB) baseline, A100(40GB) as parity, and an optimized L4/4-bit quantized variant for cost comparison. We'll provide expected reserved throughput targets for each SKU after initial bench runs.

Next steps I suggest:
- You: share a sample load profile (token distribution and session patterns) and any night/day variance we should mimic.
- Us: run an initial sizing bench, return a validation matrix with expected reserved throughput and cost delta.
- Align on SOW and pilot timeline (target: 2-week pilot starting mid-Nov).

Attachments: none from our side in this message — please attach the load profile you referenced.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Ben into the technical plan.

—
Karthik Iyer

karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Alice Ramos <alice@orbithealth.com>

Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@orbithealth.com>, OrbitHealth SRE <sre-team@orbithealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary and checklist. Confirming that the acceptance targets look reasonable to our stakeholders; a couple of clarifications and additions from our side:

1) The P95 target you listed is acceptable, but we need to explicitly capture our production 99.9 percentile SLA for critical paths — we are OK with P99 at 600 ms during the pilot provided we see clear mitigation steps for any excursions.
2) Streaming token latency: the most sensitive use case is the clinician typing assistant; if token-increment latency exceeds 70 ms under load we surface UX jitter. 55 ms target is preferred — we can sign off if median <= 30 ms and P95 <= 55 ms.
3) Data residency: pilot must run in us-west (we cannot use eu nodes for this pilot).
4) Security: attaching our security questionnaire 'security-qa.pdf' — we expect SOC2 evidence and a simple network diagram for the dedicated stack.
5) Load profile: attaching orbit-load-profile-v2.csv (columns: local-time, concurrent_sessions, avg_tokens, burst_factor). This includes a 10-minute microburst pattern we want you to replicate.

Attachments: orbit-load-profile-v2.csv, security-qa.pdf

We’ll plan for a 2-week pilot but would like the initial bench and matrix in 4 business days so we can review internally. Also please include cost delta for reserved throughput per GPU SKU in the matrix.

Thanks — Alice

--
Alice Ramos
Head of Product | OrbitHealth
alice@orbithealth.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alice Ramos <alice@orbithealth.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria & next steps (post-demo)

Looping in technical detail and a proposed validation matrix. This is written as a short runbook we’ll follow once we have your load profile (thanks — received).

Validation matrix (what we'll measure per SKU):
- Steady-state tokens/sec (with typical 150-token request distribution)
- P50/P95/P99 E2E latency (whole request)
- Streaming incremental token latency (token-to-token)
- KV cache warm vs cold effect (latency delta)
- CPU/GPU utilization profiles and memory pressure (KV cache use)
- Cost per 1M tokens (estimated) and reserved throughput slot price delta

SKUs & initial hypotheses:
- H100 80GB (fp16 + nf4): baseline for highest throughput and lowest tail variance. Expect best p99 but highest cost.
- A100 40GB (fp16 + int8 paths): similar median but likely higher p99 under concurrency due to smaller memory headroom; good parity if we shard differently.
- L4/Quantized 4-bit: cost-optimized variant for less demanding paths — lower per-token cost, higher median latency but acceptable for non-critical workloads.

Suggested sizing quick-sweep (what we’ll run in the first 4 business days):
A) Microbench: single-GPU token/sec sweep (1–8 concurrent streams) — output expected reserved tokens/sec for baseline.
B) Concurrency sweep: ramp concurrent sessions to 60+, run 30m windows to measure p95 drift.
C) Streaming probe: measure token-increment at 10k token events and with KV cache warm/cold.
D) Soak test: 6h run at 60% reserved throughput, capture resource variance and any GC/paging events.

Deliverables we’ll send back in 4 business days:
- validation-matrix.xlsx (per-SKU numbers, expected reserved-throughput targets, cost deltas)
- short writeup with recommended pilot SKU and suggested reserved concurrency/slots
- bench logs + flamegraphs (if any hotspot appears)

Attachment: validation-matrix.xlsx (placeholder — final will include numbers).

Owner: Marissa (solutions engineering) — I’ll coordinate the bench schedule with Ben (ops) and Karthik for scheduling.

Questions for OrbitHealth:
- Confirm the microburst pattern in the attached CSV is the highest priority to replicate.
- Any simulated backend latency we should include between Redwood and your app for end-to-end measurement?

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks all — this plan looks good. Quick summary and concrete next steps so we’re aligned: 

1) OrbitHealth: thanks for the load profile and security doc — we’ll mirror the microburst and day/night variance exactly in the bench. Please confirm whether the microburst should include backend RTT of 40–80ms (we can emulate it).
2) Redwood (Marissa/Ben): run the quick-sweep tests (A–D) and deliver the validation-matrix.xlsx and bench artifacts within 4 business days. Include expected reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and a recommended SKU with cost delta.
3) Karthik: I’ll draft an SOW for the 2-week pilot and share a DocuSign link for review. Draft SOW attached: pilot-sow-draft.docx.

Timing: if we start the bench Monday (Nov 9), you should have the matrix back by end-of-day Thursday (Nov 12) and the SOW signed the following week to start the pilot on Nov 23.

If that timeline works, we’ll lock Ben on the bench schedule and Marissa will own the test run.

Best —
